details.summary: On the isolated PC link, ram106 applied and renewed the DHCP address 10.77.10.10/24 while keeping 10.77.10.11/24 as an independent RAM rescue address.
hardware_checks: Both 10.77.10.10 and 10.77.10.11 present before and after forced DHCP renewal
udhcpc renewed with server 10.77.10.1 and retained the 12-hour lease
Key-authenticated SSH reached the same boot through the separate rescue address
Qt PID 126 stayed alive and the nowayout watchdog kept feeding
eMMC remained read-only and unmounted; no default route was installed
details.display_test: No display blank/unblank cycles or Qt restarts were performed; the kernel display DTB and Qt binary were inherited from ram105.
details.recovery: One-shot U-Boot restored factory p8 before kernel handoff. Requested recovery returned to healthy stock in 36.8 seconds, followed by the authorized ADC sensing-state postflight.
limitations: The DHCP application script intentionally accepts only the PC's fixed isolated lease and rejects router/DNS options; production LAN configuration and lease-loss handling are not yet qualified.
CPU1/SMP, rail policy, suspend, remote cores and SGX remain unqualified; SGX work is parked.
details.first_attempt: The first ram106 boot applied the lease, but a missing ram106 entry in the host RAM identity table caused a controller timeout. Watchdog recovery, factory p8 and manual authorized ADC postflight passed. The identity check now derives the version from the marker and has regression tests; this clean second boot is the qualification run.
